display.purpose: Masthead "STRONGSUIT" only. Fills viewport width on first load; scales fluidly on smaller screens.

tagline.purpose: "Dress your agent for the occasion." Italic, always gold, positioned below masthead.

headline.purpose: Section titles ("Look 01 Coding", "The fitting"). Gold label above in Archivo uppercase.

body.purpose: Prose paragraphs and standfirst text. Max-width 68ch for readability. Warm cream (#efe9db) on dark backgrounds.

label.purpose: Category markers ("Look 01", "Care label"). Always gold on dark, or dark on cream/gold backgrounds. Uppercase, tracked.

mono.purpose: Terminal examples, code snippets, inline code. Never for prose or UI labels. System stack (SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas).

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The one authored animation. Looks settle in opacity and translateY on scroll via animation-timeline: view(). Entry 0%–42% for body, 8%–50% for spec strips. Respects prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Look grids stack to single column. Spec strips max 26rem width. Logo moves from absolute to static.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Nav and CTA gaps reduce. Terminal blocks and buttons shrink. Font sizes remain fluid via clamp().

components.name: Button Primary
components.description: Bold, uppercase gold button. Strategic accent for CTAs.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-block; background: #e0a82e; color: #0d0c0a; font-family: 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.9rem; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; text-decoration: none; padding: 0.95rem 2.2rem; border: none; border-radius: 0; transition: background 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), transform 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { background: #f0bd4a; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #e0a82e; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Button Ghost
components.description: Secondary CTA with gold underline. Lower visual weight than primary button.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { font-family: 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; text-decoration: none; color: rgba(239, 233, 219, 0.7); border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(224, 168, 46, 0.28); padding-bottom: 2px; transition: color 160ms, border-color 160ms; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover, .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { color: #e0a82e; border-bottom-color: #e0a82e; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #e0a82e; outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview: The strongsuit landing is designed as a fashion collection lookbook, treating agent customization like tailored suiting. The visual world is deliberately print-influenced: near-black grounds anchor gold accents that own complete sections, cream paper spec strips mimic garment tags, and a single typeface pairing (Bodoni Moda + Archivo) carries both editorial presence and functional clarity. The form refuses the dark-SaaS formula (hero + six feature cards) in favor of a narrative sequence of three numbered "Looks" showing real usage patterns, with a front-and-center "care label" stating honest limits before features. Flat surfaces, hairline borders, and tonal layering replace shadows—a print grammar applied to web.
keyCharacteristics: Print-influenced grid and fabric treatment (spec strips as garment tags)
Gold accent is precious and rare (~10% of surface area)
Two-tone structure: dark backgrounds with cream spec strips, or full-spread gold sections
Honest-limits-first content ordering (care label before features)
Fluid typography that scales with viewport; no fixed breakpoints in the type itself

rules.name: The Rare Accent Rule
rules.body: Gold is strategic, not ambient. It lives in section labels, taglines, CTA buttons, and as full-spread backgrounds (Looks 02, for instance). Nowhere else. The rarity keeps it memorable and signals genuine interaction points.

rules.name: The Spec-Strip Rule
rules.body: Cream paper sections (the care label, spec metadata in the looks) are always visually separated as horizontal bands with dashed left/right borders, mimicking garment labels. These break the dark-gold pattern and introduce a distinct, supporting voice.

rules.name: The Typeface Commitment Rule
rules.body: Bodoni Moda is non-negotiable for display and primary headlines. It carries the editorial voice and print identity. Archivo is the workhorse; all UI labels, body prose, and functional text use it (never mixing serif for body). Mono is reserved for code blocks and terminal output—never for prose or labels.

rules.name: The Fluid Scale Rule
rules.body: All display and headline sizes use `clamp()` with viewport-responsive minimums and maximums. No media-query breakpoints for type. Labels and body prose are similarly fluid to maintain rhythm across all viewport sizes.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: The system is entirely flat. Depth comes from background color change, opacity variation, and hairline borders—the print grammar of a lookbook. Hover states on buttons use `transform: translateY(-1px)` for a subtle lift, but never `box-shadow`.

rules.name: The Hair-Border Rule
rules.body: Section dividers and subtle boundaries are 1px solid in cream at 16% opacity (`rgba(243, 236, 220, 0.16)`). Stronger accent borders use gold at 28% opacity. No gradient or feathered edges.

dos: Do use Bodoni Moda for all display and headline copy. Its Didone weight carries the editorial voice.
Do use gold for strategic accents only: section labels, taglines, CTA buttons, and as full-spread background colors on alternating Looks. Never more than ~10% of any surface.
Do add hairline borders (1px) in cream at 16% opacity to separate major sections and create vertical rhythm.
Do use the spec strip (cream paper card with dashed borders and anchor dot) for metadata and supporting detail. It is the signature component.
Do keep prose max-width at 68ch for readability. Use `clamp()` for all type sizes to maintain fluid scaling across viewports.
Do use cream (#efe9db) for text on dark backgrounds, not pure white. It pairs with the gold and warm paper tones.
Do apply the one authored motion moment: looks settle in on scroll via `animation-timeline: view()` with a subtle opacity and translateY. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: Don't add drop shadows or `box-shadow` anywhere. The system is flat with tonal layering only.
Don't use monospace font for prose, labels, or UI text. Mono is reserved for terminal examples and code snippets.
Don't mix rounded corners across components. Keep corners sharp (0px) except for 3px on inline code tags.
Don't use more than the committed typeface pair (Bodoni Moda + Archivo). No display sans-serif.
Don't apply transitions or animations to anything except buttons (on background/transform) and the scroll-triggered settle animation on Looks. No slide-ins, no fade-in cascade.

Don't increase the color palette. The nine named colors (ink, ink-light, gold, gold-deep, paper, paper-ink, text variants, thread, hair) are the complete system. No secondary or tertiary accent colors.
Don't break the print grammar by using GUIs, bevels, gradients, or depth effects. The aesthetic is flat and editorial.
